consumer: The engine's NPC trade/barter interaction (trade()/trade_ui input loop) asks: which items does the player select to give and take, and does the NPC accept the exchange at its computed valuation?
scope: The full interactive trade transaction between avatar and shopkeeper NPC — item selection on both sides plus the NPC's accept/reject driven through the real active input loop, not a one-sided static inventory readout.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — it merely serializes the avatar's wielded/worn/inventory items to JSON, a one-way snapshot of possession with no NPC, no valuation, and no exchange step.
divergence: Player carries a desired item and the snapshot lists it, but in the running trade the shopkeeper refuses (won't buy that category, or the offered value fails the NPC's price/balance check) — so the items the snapshot reports as present are not the items that can actually be traded; conversely items the NPC offers in return never appear in the avatar's carried_items at all.
